content.title: Sentence boundaries and commas
content.instructions: Each item contains ONE punctuation error: a comma splice, a run-on sentence, a sentence fragment, or a missing or misused comma. Rewrite the item correctly.

items.prompt: Many young people move to large cities to find work, this puts pressure on housing and transport.
accepted_answers: Many young people move to large cities to find work. This puts pressure on housing and transport.
Many young people move to large cities to find work; this puts pressure on housing and transport.
Many young people move to large cities to find work, which puts pressure on housing and transport.
items.model_answer: Many young people move to large cities to find work, which puts pressure on housing and transport.
items.explanation: Two independent clauses cannot be joined with only a comma — this is a comma splice. Use a full stop or a semicolon, or turn the second clause into a relative clause ('which puts pressure…').

items.prompt: The line graph shows the number of visitors to three museums between 2000 and 2020 the Science Museum was the most popular throughout the period.
accepted_answers: The line graph shows the number of visitors to three museums between 2000 and 2020. The Science Museum was the most popular throughout the period.
The line graph shows the number of visitors to three museums between 2000 and 2020; the Science Museum was the most popular throughout the period.
items.model_answer: The line graph shows the number of visitors to three museums between 2000 and 2020. The Science Museum was the most popular throughout the period.
items.explanation: This is a run-on (fused) sentence: two complete sentences with no punctuation between them. End the first sentence after '2020' or separate the clauses with a semicolon.

items.prompt: Governments should invest more in public transport. Because it reduces both congestion and air pollution.
accepted_answers: Governments should invest more in public transport because it reduces both congestion and air pollution.
Governments should invest more in public transport, as it reduces both congestion and air pollution.
items.model_answer: Governments should invest more in public transport because it reduces both congestion and air pollution.
items.explanation: A clause beginning with 'Because' is a subordinate clause and cannot stand alone as a sentence (a fragment). Attach it to the main clause; no comma is needed when 'because' comes second.

items.prompt: My hometown which is located in the north of the country has changed dramatically over the last decade.
accepted_answers: My hometown, which is located in the north of the country, has changed dramatically over the last decade.
items.model_answer: My hometown, which is located in the north of the country, has changed dramatically over the last decade.
items.explanation: A non-defining relative clause adds extra information about a noun that is already identified (the speaker has only one hometown), so it must be enclosed by a pair of commas: one before 'which' and one at the end of the clause.

items.prompt: Students, who work part-time, often achieve lower grades than those who do not.
accepted_answers: Students who work part-time often achieve lower grades than those who do not.
items.model_answer: Students who work part-time often achieve lower grades than those who do not.
items.explanation: 'Who work part-time' is a defining clause: it identifies which students are meant, so it takes no commas. With commas, the sentence would claim that all students work part-time, which contradicts 'those who do not'.

items.prompt: The number of rail passengers doubled between 2010 and 2020. Which shows that attitudes towards public transport have changed.
accepted_answers: The number of rail passengers doubled between 2010 and 2020, which shows that attitudes towards public transport have changed.
The number of rail passengers doubled between 2010 and 2020. This shows that attitudes towards public transport have changed.
items.model_answer: The number of rail passengers doubled between 2010 and 2020, which shows that attitudes towards public transport have changed.
items.explanation: A 'which' clause that comments on the whole previous idea is a relative clause, not a sentence, so it cannot follow a full stop. Join it with a comma, or start a new sentence with 'This shows…'.

items.prompt: If governments do not act now the effects of climate change will become irreversible.
accepted_answers: If governments do not act now, the effects of climate change will become irreversible.
items.model_answer: If governments do not act now, the effects of climate change will become irreversible.
items.explanation: When a subordinate clause (if, when, although, because…) comes before the main clause, put a comma at the end of it. Without the comma, 'now the effects' is momentarily misread as one phrase.

items.prompt: The proportion of elderly people living alone, rose steadily over the period.
accepted_answers: The proportion of elderly people living alone rose steadily over the period.
items.model_answer: The proportion of elderly people living alone rose steadily over the period.
items.explanation: Never put a single comma between a subject and its verb, however long the subject is. The whole phrase 'The proportion of elderly people living alone' is the subject of 'rose'.

items.prompt: Fossil fuels are running out, therefore governments must invest in renewable energy.
accepted_answers: Fossil fuels are running out; therefore, governments must invest in renewable energy.
Fossil fuels are running out. Therefore, governments must invest in renewable energy.
Fossil fuels are running out, so governments must invest in renewable energy.
items.model_answer: Fossil fuels are running out; therefore, governments must invest in renewable energy.
items.explanation: 'Therefore' is an adverb, not a conjunction, so a comma before it creates a comma splice. Use a semicolon or a full stop before it (with a comma after it), or use the conjunction 'so'.

items.prompt: Many cities now offer free activities for teenagers. Such as sports clubs, coding workshops and music lessons.
accepted_answers: Many cities now offer free activities for teenagers, such as sports clubs, coding workshops and music lessons.
items.model_answer: Many cities now offer free activities for teenagers, such as sports clubs, coding workshops and music lessons.
items.explanation: A phrase beginning with 'such as' has no main verb, so on its own it is a fragment. Attach it with a comma to the noun it gives examples of.
